newsitem.title: JAPAN: All Tokyo corn futures end up on technical buying.
newsitem.headline: All Tokyo corn futures end up on technical buying.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher in all months on Tuesday on technical buying by individual investors, but volume was thin as investors are shifting their money to other contracts, traders said.
Prices were 140 to 220 yen higher, with the benchmark March 1998 contract up 170 yen at 16,370 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 37,140 lots.

All contracts gained from the opening, despite a weaker Chicago corn market overnight, as technical buying emerged, traders said. "But volume was thin as investors are shifting money to other contracts such as soybeans," a trader said.
The spot May contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.99-1/4 per bushel at 0840 GMT, against $2.99 at Monday's close.
The spot May of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $8.33 per bushel at 0840 GMT, up from $8.31-3/4 at Monday's close.
